(literal translation) '**Golden Ball**') is an annual [football](Association_football "Association football") award presented by French news magazine *[France Football](France_Football "France Football")* since 1956. Between 2010 and 2015, in an agreement with <FIFA>, the award was temporarily merged with the [FIFA World Player of the Year](FIFA_World_Player_of_the_Year "FIFA World Player of the Year") (founded in 1991) and known as the [FIFA Ballon d'Or](FIFA_Ballon_d'Or "FIFA Ballon d'Or"). That partnership ended in 2016, and the award reverted to the Ballon d'Or, while FIFA also reverted to its own separate annual award [The Best FIFA Men's Player](The_Best_FIFA_Men's_Player "The Best FIFA Men's Player"). The recipients of the joint FIFA Ballon d'Or are considered as winners by both award organisations. The Ballon d’Or is generally regarded as football’s most prestigious and valuable individual award.[[2]](Ballon_d'Or#cite_note-2)

Conceived by sports writers [Gabriel Hanot](Gabriel_Hanot "Gabriel Hanot") and Jacques Ferran, the Ballon d'Or award honours the male player deemed to have performed the best over the previous year, based on voting by football journalists, from 1956 to 2006.[[3]](Ballon_d'Or#cite_note-:0-3) Originally, it was awarded only to players from Europe and widely known as the **European Footballer of the Year** award. In 1995, the Ballon d'Or was expanded to include all players from any origin that have been active at European clubs.[[4]](Ballon_d'Or#cite_note-Auto02-1-4)[[5]](Ballon_d'Or#cite_note-Nineties-5)

After 2007, coaches and captains of national teams were also given the right to vote.[[3]](Ballon_d'Or#cite_note-:0-3) The award became a global prize in 2007 with all professional footballers from around the world being eligible.[[6]](Ballon_d'Or#cite_note-Auto02-2-6) In 2022, France Football modified the rules for the Ballon d'Or. They changed the timing so that awards were given not for achievements during a calendar year, but for a football season.[[7]](Ballon_d'Or#cite_note-lequipe.fr-7) It was also decided that only those countries in the top 100 of the [FIFA World Ranking](FIFA_Men's_World_Ranking "FIFA Men's World Ranking") would be allowed to vote.[[7]](Ballon_d'Or#cite_note-lequipe.fr-7)

[Stanley Matthews](Stanley_Matthews "Stanley Matthews") of England was the inaugural winner of the Ballon d'Or.[[8]](Ballon_d'Or#cite_note-one-8) Prior to 2007, the award was generally known as the continental European Footballer of the Year award in English language and much international media.
